assumptions.observed_anchor: FY26 Q4 owner repricing preceded tenant repricing. In currentFY27 management expects existing-stock cost inflation to be offset, without quantified recovery achieved or timing. New stock is selected for gross profit; no multi-year matched-cohort series disclosed.
assumptions.derivation: Retain100% eventual yen-level recovery as the commercial anchor, but recognize50% of each annual owner-unit-cost increment in the year it arises and the other50% next year. This is an approximately six-month lag proxy if increases arise around the year start and tenant adjustments phase through the year. It is an annual convention, not a measured contract-renewal schedule. No percentage-margin preservation, discretionary mix uplift or unquantified prior-year catch-up.
assumptions.reason_for_base: The actual cost-before-price sequence disproves automatic simultaneous pass-through, while management’s concrete FY27 outlook supports recovery rather than permanent arbitrary spread erosion. A six-month central recognition delay represents ongoing negotiation and tenant-change opportunities; it is a house estimate bracketed by immediate and twelve-month delay tests. Eventual full recovery across future aggregate mix remains conditional and is tested at75%,50%,0%. No contractual automatic escalator or guarantee is claimed.
assumptions.timing: Half current-year increment plus half prior-year increment; first year excludes an unmeasured FY26 catch-up. Fully effective level recovery follows one year later, not full same-year earnings recovery. New cohorts are priced through the same aggregate proxy, a material simplification.
assumptions.alternative: Immediate full recovery;75% eventual recovery with six-month lag;50% eventual with lag;zero recovery;100% eventual with twelve-month lag. Bear combines50% eventual with lag and other weaker operating inputs.
assumptions.range: Eventual recovery0–100%; recognition0–100% in year of rise; base eventual100%/current-year50%.
assumptions.falsifier: Existing-tenant rent revision fails to match owner increases over subsequent renewals; churn rises when rents increase; new inventory economics deteriorate; achieved pricing evidence requires a different lag.
assumptions.mechanism: Owner rent is paid on all average contracted spaces. Tenant service yield receives only the recognized increment per occupied space at fixed reference occupancy. The remaining increment is carried into the following year. Dollar recovery preserves yen spread before other costs, not margin percentage.
